document: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act), as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI)
article_or_section_as_coded: Article 9(1)-(9) (Chapter III, Section 2) – Risk management system
page_number_as_coded: Consolidated pp. 21-22 (Art. 9 begins p. 21); original OJ pp. 56-57
exact_text_as_coded: A risk management system shall be established, implemented, documented and maintained in relation to high-risk AI systems.
provision_summary_as_coded: Providers must run a documented, continuous and iterative risk management process across the whole lifecycle of a high-risk AI system. It covers identifying and analysing known and reasonably foreseeable risks to health, safety or fundamental rights, estimating risks under intended use and reasonably foreseeable misuse, evaluating risks from post-market monitoring data, and adopting targeted mitigation measures so that residual risk is judged acceptable. Systems must be tested, including before being placed on the market, against prior defined metrics and probabilistic thresholds (Art. 9(6)-(8)). Providers must consider likely adverse impacts on persons under 18 and other vulnerable groups (Art. 9(9)).
responsible_party_as_coded: AI provider (of high-risk AI systems)
applicability_as_coded: High-risk AI systems (classified under Art. 6 and Annexes I/III). Risks covered are limited to those that can be reasonably mitigated or eliminated through development, design or adequate technical information (Art. 9(3)). Art. 9(9) requires consideration of impacts on persons under 18 and other vulnerable groups.
enforcement_mechanism_as_coded: Art. 16(a) (cons. p. 28; OJ p. 62) obliges providers to ensure compliance with Chapter III Section 2 (Arts 8-15). Non-compliance with Art. 16 provider obligations is subject to administrative fines of up to EUR 15 000 000 or, if the offender is an undertaking, up to 3% of total worldwide annual turnover for the preceding financial year, whichever is higher (Art. 99(4)(a), cons. p. 116; OJ p. 115; unchanged by 2026/1744). For SMEs, including start-ups, the lower of the two applies (Art. 99(6), OJ p. 116). The Act sets maxima; Member States lay down the penalty rules and enforce them (Art. 99(1), OJ p. 115). Ex ante conformity assessment (Art. 43, cons. p. 53; OJ p. 78); market surveillance (Art. 74, cons. p. 91; OJ p. 102) and procedure for AI systems presenting a risk (Art. 79, cons. p. 104; OJ p. 106).

document: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act), as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI)
article_or_section_as_coded: Article 13(1)-(3) (Chapter III, Section 2) – Transparency and provision of information to deployers
page_number_as_coded: Consolidated pp. 25-26 (Art. 13 begins p. 25); original OJ pp. 59-60
exact_text_as_coded: High-risk AI systems shall be designed and developed in such a way as to ensure that their operation is sufficiently transparent to enable deployers to interpret a system’s output and use it appropriately.
provision_summary_as_coded: High-risk AI systems must be transparent enough for deployers to interpret their outputs and use them appropriately. They must come with instructions for use giving concise, complete, correct and clear information. At minimum this includes the provider's identity, the system's intended purpose, its capabilities and limitations, its accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity levels, foreseeable risk circumstances, any capabilities for explaining outputs, human oversight measures, maintenance needs and log-handling mechanisms.
responsible_party_as_coded: AI provider (information duty owed to deployers)
applicability_as_coded: High-risk AI systems. The beneficiary of the information is the deployer, not end-users or affected persons. Transparency towards natural persons interacting with AI systems (e.g. chatbots, deepfakes) is a separate regime under Art. 50. Affected persons have a separate right to obtain explanations of individual decisions from the deployer (Art. 86, OJ p. 110).
enforcement_mechanism_as_coded: Art. 16(a) (cons. p. 28; OJ p. 62) obliges providers to ensure compliance with Chapter III Section 2 (Arts 8-15). Non-compliance with Art. 16 provider obligations is subject to administrative fines of up to EUR 15 000 000 or, if the offender is an undertaking, up to 3% of total worldwide annual turnover for the preceding financial year, whichever is higher (Art. 99(4)(a), cons. p. 116; OJ p. 115; unchanged by 2026/1744). For SMEs, including start-ups, the lower of the two applies (Art. 99(6), OJ p. 116). The Act sets maxima; Member States lay down the penalty rules and enforce them (Art. 99(1), OJ p. 115). Ex ante conformity assessment (Art. 43, cons. p. 53; OJ p. 78); market surveillance (Art. 74, cons. p. 91; OJ p. 102) and procedure for AI systems presenting a risk (Art. 79, cons. p. 104; OJ p. 106). Deployers must use systems in accordance with the instructions for use (Art. 26(1); Art. 26 begins cons. p. 37), with deployer breaches finable under Art. 99(4)(e).

document: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act), as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI)
article_or_section_as_coded: Article 14(1)-(4) (Chapter III, Section 2) – Human oversight
page_number_as_coded: Consolidated pp. 26-27 (Art. 14 begins p. 26); original OJ pp. 60-61
exact_text_as_coded: High-risk AI systems shall be designed and developed in such a way, including with appropriate human-machine interface tools, that they can be effectively overseen by natural persons during the period in which they are in use.
provision_summary_as_coded: High-risk AI systems must be designed so that natural persons can effectively oversee them while in use, with the aim of preventing or minimising risks to health, safety or fundamental rights. Oversight measures must be proportionate to risk, autonomy and context, and may be built in by the provider or identified by the provider for the deployer to implement. The system must be provided to the deployer so that the people assigned to oversight are enabled, as appropriate and proportionate, to understand its capacities and limitations, remain aware of automation bias, interpret its outputs, decide not to use or to override an output, and stop the system safely (Art. 14(4)).
responsible_party_as_coded: AI provider (design obligation); AI deployer (implementation, via Art. 26(2))
applicability_as_coded: High-risk AI systems. Additional two-person verification rule for remote biometric identification systems (Annex III point 1(a)), with an exception for law enforcement, migration, border control or asylum where Union or national law deems it disproportionate (Art. 14(5)).
enforcement_mechanism_as_coded: Art. 16(a) (cons. p. 28; OJ p. 62) obliges providers to ensure compliance with Chapter III Section 2 (Arts 8-15). Non-compliance with Art. 16 provider obligations is subject to administrative fines of up to EUR 15 000 000 or, if the offender is an undertaking, up to 3% of total worldwide annual turnover for the preceding financial year, whichever is higher (Art. 99(4)(a), cons. p. 116; OJ p. 115; unchanged by 2026/1744). For SMEs, including start-ups, the lower of the two applies (Art. 99(6), OJ p. 116). The Act sets maxima; Member States lay down the penalty rules and enforce them (Art. 99(1), OJ p. 115). Ex ante conformity assessment (Art. 43, cons. p. 53; OJ p. 78); market surveillance (Art. 74, cons. p. 91; OJ p. 102) and procedure for AI systems presenting a risk (Art. 79, cons. p. 104; OJ p. 106). Deployers must assign human oversight to natural persons with the necessary competence, training and authority (Art. 26(2); Art. 26 begins cons. p. 37, OJ p. 68 for para. 2; unchanged by 2026/1744); breach finable under Art. 99(4)(e).

article_or_section_as_coded: Rule 3(3) (Due diligence in relation to synthetically generated information), clauses (a) and (b); read with rule 4(1A) for significant social media intermediaries
page_number_as_coded: Rule-level pinpoint; PDF page not yet verified
exact_text_as_coded: (3) Due diligence in relation to synthetically generated information … it deploys reasonable and appropriate technical measures, … to not allow any user to create … every such information not covered under sub-clause (i) of clause (a) is prominently labelled … shall be embedded with a permanent metadata or other appropriate technical provenance mechanisms … the intermediary shall not enable the modification, suppression or removal of the label, permanent metadata
provision_summary_as_coded: Intermediaries whose services enable the creation or dissemination of synthetically generated information (SGI) must use reasonable technical measures to prevent unlawful SGI, label lawful SGI prominently, embed permanent metadata or other provenance mechanisms, and prevent labels and metadata from being removed. Significant social media intermediaries must also require users to declare whether content is SGI, verify declarations with technical measures and display a label where content is confirmed as SGI (rule 4(1A)).

Applies to intermediaries under the IT Act, 2000; additional duties for significant social media intermediaries.
enforcement_mechanism_as_coded: Due-diligence obligation under the IT Rules: under rule 7, if an intermediary fails to observe the Rules, 'the provisions of sub-section (1) of section 79 of the Act shall not be applicable to such intermediary' (loss of safe-harbour protection), exposing it to liability under the IT Act and other law. Takedown and blocking powers under the IT Act also apply.
